Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Comparing corresponding visible closure features of the same woman's jacket in the source and edited images, is there visible progress toward bringing the front panels together, although the jacket is not fully closed?
node.criteria: Pass only if corresponding visible closure features show movement toward bringing the front panels together, while the jacket remains not fully closed. Fail only if those features can be compared reliably and show no such progress. Unknown if pose, occlusion, or draping prevents a reliable comparison; do not infer progress or its absence from pose or silhouette alone.
node.binding: Compare the same woman's jacket in the source and edited images. Focus on visible front edges, their separation, and any fastener or closure area. Account for pose changes only insofar as the same closure features remain comparable; disregard unrelated edits.

node_traces.evidence: The woman's pose and jacket draping differ substantially between images. The front closure features are not reliably comparable, so visible progress toward closing the jacket cannot be established.

fulfillment: The endpoint check is well grounded: the edited jacket is visibly open, so keep that failure. The unresolved result comes from the progress comparison, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure: both supports were valid and queried, but support 2 treats pose and drape differences as making comparison unreliable. Refine the binding/criteria for support 2 to compare only jacket-closure evidence that remains observable across views (for example, whether the front panels or opening have moved toward closure), while allowing unknown when that evidence genuinely cannot be aligned. Do not infer progress merely from the changed pose or jacket appearance. The reference label is an aggregate constraint, not proof of a particular atomic finding; investigate whether the visible edited jacket provides comparable evidence of any closure progress before changing the outcome. Preserve the distinction between fully closed, partial progress, no progress, and unresolved, and do not weaken the complete-closure requirement.
